sealed_candidate.answer: ## Recommendation: Declared outcome + matched comparison, not accepted-PR counts **Bottom line:** The only decision-grade way to judge agent productivity is a **matched-task comparison** against a defined baseline, scored on quality, human review time, rework, elapsed lead time, total cost, and failed/abandoned work. **The supplied evidence cannot support a productivity conclusion today.** ### Why the accepted-PR figure is not a valid outcome The pilot reports **40 accepted pull requests in one month**, but provides **no task mix, control group, reviewer hours, failure count, or provider costs** [measurement-context]. The measurement policy explicitly instructs that causal benefit must **not** be inferred from accepted-PR counts [measurement-policy]. These two records are consistent: the policy defines the required protocol, and the context confirms the pilot does not meet it. ### Required accounting boundary Before any conclusion, declare: 1. **Outcome:** quality-gated delivery (accepted *and* surviving review), not raw acceptance. 2. **Comparison:** matched tasks against a human (or pre-agent) baseline with the same task class. 3. **Accounting boundary:** human review time, rework, failed/abandoned tasks, elapsed lead time, and total provider cost [measurement-policy]. ### Unresolved limits (explicitly open) - **Missing baseline** — no control group exists in the pilot note. - **Missing task mix** — acceptance counts may be dominated by easy tasks. - **Missing failure count** — abandoned work is unmeasured. - **Missing cost and review-time data** — total cost of delivery is unknown. - **Time horizon** — one month cannot establish sustained productivity. Per the abstention rule, no productivity verdict is drawn; the pilot as recorded cannot support the decision.
